facts.text: ALSEP Central Station was deployed at Ocean of Storms during Apollo 12 in 1969.

The Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package — a suite of scientific instruments powered by a plutonium-238 RTG. Included a seismometer, magnetometer, solar wind spectrometer, and more. Transmitted data to Earth until September 1977.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Its seismometer detected the deliberate crash of the Intrepid ascent stage, producing vibrations that rang for nearly an hour — revealing the Moon's highly fractured upper crust.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Ocean of Storms.
Transmitted data continuously for nearly eight years until NASA shut down all ALSEP stations on 30 September 1977 to save budget.
